items.headline: SimplyGo fixes glitch that denied a 50-cent pre-peak discount on 210,000 trips a day
items.summary: A configuration error meant the S$0.50 pre-peak rail discount was not applied on Aug 20 and 21, affecting about 210,000 journeys a day; SimplyGo flagged it Aug 21 and said it was resolved.

items.headline: Town council managing-agent employee, 63, charged with taking S$220,000 in bribes
items.summary: The employee was charged on Aug 21 with taking about S$220,000 in bribes from company directors, allegedly buying a Mercedes-Benz; three other men were also charged.

items.headline: Police patrol car catches fire on the BKE; two traffic officers taken to hospital
items.summary: A traffic police vehicle caught fire about 12.10am on Aug 21 on the BKE towards Woodlands; two officers were treated for smoke inhalation and discharged, cause under investigation.

items.headline: Yishun jewellery store manager who swapped S$216,000 of gold for Taobao copies jailed
items.summary: Darren Wai Mun Jun, 31, stole 24 gold pieces worth S$216,613 from a Northpoint City jeweller and replaced several with Taobao copies, disabling CCTV; jailed two years, four months and two weeks.

items.headline: Update: Elderly hawker, 73, with a fractured back after Roxy Square shove says he forgives his attacker
items.summary: After being thrown to the floor on Aug 15 and fracturing his back, the 73-year-old hawker said on Aug 22 he forgives the man, who has apologised, and will not pursue the matter.

items.headline: Assam monsoon floods kill at least 87 and affect more than a million people
items.summary: An Al Jazeera report says Assam's monsoon floods have killed at least 87, including about 47 in Sivasagar district, and affected over a million; opposition lawmakers allege illegal riverbed excavation worsened it.

items.headline: India allows duty-free raw sugar imports in a rare move to cool record domestic prices
items.summary: The commerce ministry cleared up to one million tonnes of tax-free raw sugar imports until Oct 31, waiving the 100% levy, after domestic prices hit a record.

items.headline: India's growth may beat the RBI's 6.7% forecast and near 7%, deputy governor says
items.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said full-year growth through March could approach 7%, above the central bank's 6.7% projection, citing a strong April-June quarter.

items.headline: India's NSE seeks up to $55 billion valuation in what would be the country's biggest IPO
items.summary: The National Stock Exchange is marketing shares at 2,000-2,100 rupees, implying about 5.26 trillion rupees (~$55bn); the ~6% stake could raise ~315bn rupees, launching in the second half of September.

items.headline: Palestinian-British girl, 6, dies days after her family drowned off the Sussex coast
items.summary: Saja el-Khawas has died, Sussex Police said Aug 22; her father, mother and 14-year-old sister died at the scene after getting into difficulty in the water at Shoreham on Aug 18.

items.headline: UK private sector grows at its fastest pace in four months as spending picks up
items.summary: S&P Global's flash composite PMI rose to 52.5 in August, a four-month high, as households and firms spent more, pointing to steady third-quarter growth.

items.headline: UK labour market weakens further as price pressures mount
items.summary: Fresh data showed Britain's jobs market softening while inflation accelerated for the first time in four months on higher energy and electronics costs, complicating the Bank of England's path.

items.headline: El Nino set to be the most intense in more than a century, UK forecasters warn
items.summary: UK forecasters said the current El Nino is expected to be the strongest in over a hundred years, after Britain's record-dry July and repeated heatwaves.

items.headline: Russian 'double-tap' drone strike on a Kryvyi Rih shopping mall kills at least 14
items.summary: Two waves of drones hit a large mall in Kryvyi Rih on Aug 21, the second reportedly targeting rescuers; at least 14 were killed and around 130 wounded, with the toll rising. Zelenskyy called it a terrorist act.

items.headline: Update: Iran's president says it is time to end the war with the US 'from a position of strength'
items.summary: President Masoud Pezeshkian called on Aug 22 for an end to the war with the United States, saying Tehran negotiates from strength as talks stall; Washington has threatened its toughest-ever sanctions.

items.headline: First US deportees arrive in Liberia; five who refused are flown on to Equatorial Guinea
items.summary: Twenty deportees landed near Monrovia on Aug 20, the first of up to 1,200 under a US-funded deal; five who refused were flown against their will to Equatorial Guinea, the first onward diversion in the programme.

items.headline: UK, Canada and Australia condemn Israel for closing its World Central Kitchen strike probe
items.summary: After Israel declined to investigate the April 2024 strike that killed seven WCK aid workers, the three governments called the decision shameful on Aug 21; Poland and Australia summoned Israel's ambassadors.

items.headline: Yemen slides toward full-scale war as Houthis claim drone strikes on Najran and an Aramco site
items.summary: Yemen's government and the Houthis traded heavy attacks; the government claimed 81 operations in 24 hours and Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said two drones struck Najran province on Aug 20. Riyadh gave no confirmation.

items.headline: TikTok and ByteDance to pay $400 million to settle a US children's-privacy lawsuit
items.summary: TikTok agreed to pay $400 million to resolve a DOJ suit alleging it let under-13 users onto the platform and collected their data in violation of COPPA; it will add stronger age and parental controls.

items.headline: Apple cuts more than 200 jobs across its Siri, Vision Pro and AI teams
items.summary: Apple confirmed cuts of over 200 roles, roughly 100 from Vision Pro and about 100 from the Siri and Intelligent Systems Experience groups, as it refocuses on new devices and AI.

items.headline: Anthropic hires a Google chip veteran as it lays the groundwork for its own AI silicon
items.summary: Anthropic hired Amir Salek, a founder of Google's custom-chip program who ran its TPU business until 2022, for its compute team as it moves to co-design its own AI semiconductors.

items.headline: Nvidia is in talks with Korean AI-chip startup Rebellions over a possible deal
items.summary: Nvidia is in early talks with Rebellions, a Korean inference-chip designer founded in 2020, about a partnership, investment or acquisition; Rebellions last raised $400 million pre-IPO.

items.headline: Junk-bond investors pile into investment-grade AI data-center debt
items.summary: High-yield buyers are moving into higher-rated AI data-center bonds, with QTS Realty selling $3.9 billion for a Microsoft-linked Georgia facility at yields near 7.23%.

items.headline: Gold hits a three-month high as a US Treasury buyback plan revives debasement fears
items.summary: Spot gold rose about 1.6% on Aug 21 to around $4,590 an ounce, its highest since mid-May and up ~5% on the week, after the Treasury signalled a bigger buyback of long-dated debt.

items.headline: Japan's core inflation accelerates to 1.8% in July, strengthening the case for a BOJ hike
items.summary: Core CPI excluding fresh food rose 1.8% year on year in July, up from 1.6%, as firms passed on weak-yen costs; markets expect the Bank of Japan to raise its rate to 1.25% in September.

items.headline: Holcim to buy Fermacell from James Hardie for 840 million euros
items.summary: Holcim agreed to acquire Fermacell, James Hardie's European walling and flooring business with ~430m euros in sales and 1,000+ staff; the deal should close in the first half of 2027.

items.headline: Ross Stores tops estimates on tariff refunds as shares jump about 8%
items.summary: Ross Stores posted earnings of $2.66 a share, well above guidance, lifted by IEEPA tariff refunds, with comparable-store sales up 10%; it raised its outlook and shares rose ~8%.

items.headline: Russell wins the Zandvoort sprint ahead of Leclerc and Norris; Verstappen sixth
items.summary: George Russell converted sprint pole into his third sprint win of 2026, beating Charles Leclerc by 1.36s at Zandvoort, with Lando Norris third and Max Verstappen sixth at home.

items.headline: Norris denies Russell pole for the Dutch Grand Prix as rain closes in
items.summary: Lando Norris took pole for the Dutch Grand Prix with a 1:11.163, edging Russell by 0.102s as rain threatened qualifying; Antonelli qualified third and Verstappen seventh, with the race on Aug 23.

items.headline: Starc takes 6-12 and Bangladesh are bowled out for 64 on a chaotic day one at Mackay
items.summary: Mitchell Starc claimed 6-12 and Shoriful Islam 6-35 on an 18-wicket opening day of the second Test at Mackay, where Bangladesh were dismissed for 64 before Australia built a lead.

items.headline: Arthur Fils beats Cobolli to reach his first Masters 1000 final in Cincinnati
items.summary: Arthur Fils won a rain-delayed semi-final against Flavio Cobolli 6-3, 6-4 in 67 minutes to reach his maiden ATP Masters 1000 final, days before the US Open.

items.headline: JWST finds hidden faint stars make the first galaxies three to four times more massive
items.summary: Astronomers studying nine early massive quiescent galaxies combined JWST spectra with ground data and found a bottom-heavy population of low-mass stars, making some galaxies 3-4x more massive than thought.

items.headline: Experiment pins a mysterious low-energy gamma-ray glow in atomic nuclei to a magnetic effect
items.summary: A large international team showed the long-puzzling low-energy enhancement in the gamma-ray strength function of zinc-70 is magnetic in origin, sharpening models of how heavy elements form in stars.

items.headline: Antarctica's recent ice-sheet gain was a temporary anomaly, not a new normal, study finds
items.summary: A study published Aug 19 in Nature links Antarctica's 2021-2023 mass gain to unusually heavy snowfall driven by a warm patch of tropical ocean; such anomalies recur about once a decade and the ice sheet should resume losing mass.

fun_fact.headline: A teaspoon of neutron-star material would weigh about a billion tonnes.
fun_fact.body: A single teaspoon of neutron-star material would weigh roughly a billion tonnes on Earth, about the mass of a mountain. Neutron stars are so dense that more than the entire mass of the Sun is squeezed into a sphere only about 20 kilometres across.

puzzle.title: The Painted Cube
puzzle.body: A wooden 3x3x3 cube is painted red on all six outer faces, then sliced into 27 unit cubes. (a) How many small cubes have paint on exactly two faces? (b) How many have no paint at all?
puzzle.approach: Picture where each small cube sits (corner, edge, face-centre, or centre) and count exposed faces.
puzzle.answer: (a) 12 edge cubes have exactly two painted faces; (b) 1 core cube has none. Breakdown: 8 corners (3 faces), 12 edges (2), 6 face-centres (1), 1 core (0).

word_puzzle.title: Four of a Kind
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words (BAND BOUT CALL CHAIN CLINCH DIAL FLUSH FOLD HOOK JAB PENDANT RAISE RING RIVER STUD TEXT) into four groups of four.
word_puzzle.approach: Lock words that fit only one category first, then let the counts force the traps (CALL, RING, STUD, FLUSH).
word_puzzle.answer: Poker: FLUSH FOLD RAISE RIVER; Phone: CALL DIAL RING TEXT; Jewellery: BAND CHAIN PENDANT STUD; Boxing: BOUT CLINCH HOOK JAB.

notes: Sourcing constraint: the compute environment's crawler could not reach several allowed outlets directly (BBC, Sky News, Reuters, AP, The Guardian, New Scientist, and India's primary outlets), and WebFetch to article bodies was egress-blocked, so items were verified from search-result metadata across allowed outlets. India ran on fallback sources (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg) because every primary India outlet (The Hindu, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, Times of India, NDTV, Economic Times) was unreachable; 3 retry attempts were made before falling back. UK News ran on fallback sources (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg) because BBC and Sky News were unreachable. Global relied on Al Jazeera and CNN. Other Miscellaneous News carried 3 items (fewer today) because in-window, allowed-source frontier-science stories with reachable deep URLs were scarce. F1 currency confirmed against Formula1.com: Zandvoort (Dutch GP) is the current round; the sprint result and pole are reported and the Grand Prix itself runs the evening of Aug 23 SGT. No edition was skipped.
